question: The torpedo aim tick's steering delta at 009D1699 sits at 2.28-2.34 rad for the whole run while the cone flag at 009D2209 needs it far smaller, so no aircraft ever arms the release timer at 009D2287. Is the delta measured against a heading the planner does not steer, or in a different convention (compass versus mathematical, a pi or pi/2 offset, a sign flip)? Fix it at the producer.
answer: There is no convention mismatch, and the delta is correct. Slot 50h of the unit vtable is a per-family heading getter with two overrides, both two-instruction leaves. 006DFD60 BSP_UnitInstance_GetHullHeading is FLD [ECX+1050h] / RET and holds slot 50h in nine ship vtables. 0074E260 is FLD [ECX+0C6Ch] / RET and holds slot 50h in nine others, among them 00D05F20, the vtable BSP_PlaneUnitInstance_Construct (007CFD20) installs at 007CFD78; the destructor 007D03A0 re-installs the same vtable at 007D03C1. So the aim tick's CALL EDX at 009D1679 returns unit+C6Ch on an aircraft, and 00438B10 (FLD [ESP+4] / FSUB [ESP+8], RET 8) makes the delta stored at 009D1699 exactly WrapPi(approach+94h - unit+C6Ch). The pilot planner's yaw base at 0099DEB8 subtracts the same unit+C6Ch from plan+2C0h, and 009D1BCC writes plan+2C0h = WrapAdd(unit+C6Ch, delta), so the planner's heading error and the aim tick's delta are the same number by construction. Every heading on the path is the compass angle from +Z toward +X: approach+94h is pi/2 - atan2(dz, dx) at 009D35C0, unit+C6Ch is pi/2 - atan2(flat_fz, flat_fx) at 007C1900. Same zero, same sense, no offset, no sign flip. What actually blocks the drop is two things the packet brief did not have. First, the cone at 009D2209 is not a few tens of degrees: 009D21AC interpolates 80 degrees at 0.3 s down to 50 degrees at 0.8 s, and 009D21F2 interpolates 50 degrees down to 15 degrees at 1.6 s, so for every part of a run-in more than 1.6 s from the target the gate demands the nose within 0.262 rad. Second, the aircraft thrash: goaway 009D0D90 is entered 87-98 times per aircraft in 150 s, and four of the five never clear the 700.0 m break-off at +24h while in it, so the commanded heading reverses about every 1.7 s and cannot converge into a 15-degree cone whatever its convention. One real host divergence exists at this hop and is small: AimTickBinding::unit_heading_vtable50 binds the native's slot-50h call to pose_heading_radians, the producer of the SHIP field unit+1050h, rather than to unit_.plane_heading_c6c. Both reduce to atan2(fx, fz) over the same forward row, so it does not move the delta; it is a faithfulness fix and it restores 007C1900's near-vertical latch. It is stated as a contract because src/game_hosts_units.cpp was leased to agent/cc8-recon-binding for this packet's whole turn.
coverage: Two findings. The convention question is analyzed-only and closed: no reconstruction on that path is wrong. The thrash question is partly landed: torpedo_seed_run_speeds_009d0484 is reconstructed and built, but the host fix it enables is unlanded because src/game_hosts_units.cpp stayed leased elsewhere for the whole packet, so the after-run and the per-tick census are not yet measured. Complete for the vtable slot attribution of 0074E260 and 006DFD60 (all 18 occurrences of the two functions in .rdata, every one on slot 0x50), for 00438B10 read to both its RETs, for the delta production 009D15F0-009D1699 read instruction by instruction, and for the cone gate 009D2168-009D220F read to the flag store. Four of the nine vtables carrying 0074E260 are attributed to named aircraft constructors with Ghidra body ranges: 00D00070 (BSP_ReconPlaneUnitInstance_Construct), 00D00308 (BSP_LargeReconPlaneUnitInstance_Construct), 00D05F20 (BSP_PlaneUnitInstance_Construct) and 00D0BA80 (BSP_SmallReconPlaneUnitInstance_Construct). thrash_root_cause.finding: An altitude is used as the run speed. src/game_hosts_units.cpp:3105-3106 assigns kPilotTorpedoCruisingAltDefault (500.0, Pilot/Torpedo/CruisingAlt, tuning singleton +430h) to BOTH approach speed slots +80h and +7Ch. Neither +14h nor +24h is written in the body 009D0380-009D066F. 009D3445's clamp never bites because the ceiling 00CE4C04 is 9999.0.
thrash_root_cause.effect: clause 2 of the aim-complete rule is |delta| > F0C. It fires when range < 600*(|delta|-1) + speed, which at |delta| 2.28 is 1268 m with speed 500 and 890 m with the aircraft's real 122 m/s. 1268 m is exactly the F14 of 1239-1274 the run reports, so aim hands over to goaway about a kilometre too early on every cycle.
thrash_root_cause.three_arms_of_009d1500: t = range/speed returned directly when t <= 1.0 (009D154E/009D15B1); t again when speed >= the float 600.0 at 00CE4BC4 (009D1570/009D15B9); otherwise (range - speed)/600.0 + 1.0 at 009D1598-009D15A1. The reconstruction at src/torpedo_approach_update.cpp:110-125 carries all three faithfully.

break_off_is_not_the_defect.name: BSP_BotStateTorpedoGoAway_IsComplete
break_off_is_not_the_defect.finding: 009D318C FLD [ESP] (break-off state+24h), 009D318F FLD [ECX+90h] (range), 009D3195 FCOMPI ST(1), 009D3199 JBE: returns true when range > break-off, with an optional FMUL by the double 0.4 at 00CE65D0 (009D3183) behind the always-engage pair ctl+369h and [00E17BF2]. With the range at 697-766 m and the break-off at 700, goaway completes on or near the tick it is entered: Mav4 spends 87 ticks in goaway across 87 entries, one tick each. That is correct behaviour; an aircraft already outside the safe distance has nothing to go away from. The break-off quantity needs no change.
break_off_is_not_the_defect.cycle: aim for roughly fourteen arm ticks, clause 2 fires, one tick of goaway, back to the attack run. 87-98 entries per aircraft in 150 s, about one reversal every 1.7 s.
break_off_is_not_the_defect.producer: BSP_BotStateTorpedoGoAway_Enter 009D0D90-009D0F04 is the only producer of state+24h. 009D0DC1 takes the tuning singleton and 009D0DD1 reads Pilot/Torpedo/SafeDist at +438h = 700.0. When approach+CCh has a target (009D0DCF) that answers target->vtable[5Ch](5) (009D0DEA), 009D0DF2 calls 007B5BE0 for the target's largest extent and 009D0E03 takes the larger of the two. 009D0E27 pushes 1.0 and 009D0E15 pushes the float 1.15 at 00D20CE4, 009D0E2C calls 00BD2F10 UniformFloatRange, 009D0E31 multiplies the base and 009D0E37 stores state+24h. 00BD2F10 cleans its two arguments, which is why no add esp,8 follows it here or at 009D05CC. The side state+2Ch comes from 009D0DBC, -1.0 (00D7A260) or +1.0 (00D7A24C) by the parity of the global at 00F876B0.
break_off_is_not_the_defect.host_fidelity: faithful with two substitutions the host already labels at src/game_hosts_units.cpp:2970-2979: has_extent_target = false because 007B5BE0 needs approach+CCh's entity bounds, and the jitter is pinned to kDistanceJitterLo = 1.0. So the break-off is 700.0 where the native would draw 700-805. Taking the low end makes the break-off SMALLER and goaway complete SOONER, so it cannot be what keeps the aircraft cycling.
break_off_is_not_the_defect.is_plus_90h_right: yes. approach+90h is the 2D range to the target POINT that 009D35C0 also takes the bearing to, and the host builds range_90 from the same target_xz. The native compares that point range against a distance derived from the target ENTITY's extent; that is the native's own choice and the host mirrors it.

self_correction.what_was_wrong: Two claims made before measuring did not survive the per-tick census.
self_correction.1_degenerate_substitution: slot.motion.max_speed (VehicleClass+500h) is 0.0f on an aircraft. The class row exists - the run reports all 77 units carrying one - but planes take no speed from it. 009D1500's speed == 0 guard then returns F0C = 0.0000 every tick, so clause 2 fires on the FIRST aim tick. local/usn01_after.log: goaway entries 96 -> 208 per aircraft, transitions 176 -> 419. Closest approach did improve, 920.9 m -> 473.5 m, because the aircraft stop orbiting and press in, but a time-to-target of zero at 2196 m is not defensible and the value was reverted.
self_correction.2_dimensional_argument_does_not_hold: 009D1500's third arm divides by the double 600.0 at 00D20198, which is not a physical aircraft speed. F0C is an urgency number, not an ETA, and clause 2 compares it against radians. So the right magnitude for the speed slots cannot be argued from dimensions, and 500 may sit in the range the native intends. What stays true: the host takes the number from Pilot/Torpedo/CruisingAlt, an altitude constant that is not evidence for any speed, while the native takes it from an unread run profile record.
self_correction.what_the_census_settled: unit+C6Ch and the hull heading are the same number to four decimals on every census row, on all five aircraft at every sample. That confirms the rule 1 and 2 convention analysis empirically and confirms the prediction that the unit_heading_vtable50 producer fix is numerically neutral. Separately, at aim tick 51 of the degenerate run the delta was already 0.8948 rad with cone_open=1, so the cone is not the binding constraint and the nose does come round; clause 2 is what ends the run-in.

command_slot_defect.name: aim tick frame slot F=1Ch
command_slot_defect.finding: F=1Ch is seeded with approach+94h, the bearing, at 009D1622 MOVSS [ESP+1Ch],XMM0, and 009D168A reads that same slot back as the first argument of the delta's 00438B10. The only other write is 009D18A6, inside the sector-turn block that 009D1794 skips when approach+5Ch is zero. src/torpedo_aim_tick.cpp initialised it to 0.0f, so with +5Ch == 0 and the sector probe armed the fold at 009D1B7A produced f10_turn = WrapSub(WrapAdd(0, f48), heading), which with no probe hit is exactly -heading, and 009D1BCC commanded heading 0 (due +Z) instead of the bearing. Every such tick published a spurious command into plan+2C0h.
command_slot_defect.caught_by: the per-tick census added in this packet. KatTBD aim tick 51 read cmd_2C0=0.0000 with bearing_94=0.9543 and yaw_C6C=0.5963, a delta of exactly -yaw, while ticks 1 and 101 of the same aircraft were consistent. The original five-aircraft run never showed it because its scan reported 36 clear sectors of 36, so the probe was never armed.
command_slot_defect.fix: src/torpedo_aim_tick.cpp, float f1c_command = f1c_bearing, cited to 009D1622.

ghidra_state_changed_during_the_packet: Both addresses this packet reported as no_ghidra_function were defined in Ghidra by the integrator while it ran, and arrived in this worktree with the merge of main at 41eb6a7b8 (reports/torpedo_steering_delta_function_definitions.json). 0074E260 is now BSP_PlaneUnitInstance_GetHeading with body 0074E260-0074E266, which matches the inclusive end this packet reported exactly. 009D15F0 is now BSP_BotStateTorpedoAim_Tick with body 009D15F0-009D2379; this packet and the earlier aim-tick packet both reported the final RET at 009D2377, so Ghidra's end runs two bytes past it, presumably over padding. The no_ghidra_function list is therefore empty, and the call rows are now checked for containment and CALL-ness rather than skipped.

max_speed_substitution_settled.instruction: the lead asked for the speed seed to be landed from slot_.motion.max_speed as a labelled substitution
max_speed_substitution_settled.measurement: local/usn01_speeds.log, merged tree, census extended to print the candidates. On ALL NINE torpedo aircraft and BOTH classes (KatTBD, ConTBD1-3, Mav1-5): class_max_speed=0.0, stall=19.4, speed_80=500.0 (the placeholder).
max_speed_substitution_settled.conclusion: slot_.motion.max_speed is 0.0f for every torpedo aircraft in this mission, so it cannot be used. Seeding from it drives 009D1500's speed == 0 guard and returns F0C = 0.0000 on every tick, which was measured earlier on the pre-merge tree: clause 2 fired at aim tick 1 and goaway entries went 96 -> 208 per aircraft. The instruction is therefore answered with data rather than carried out.

Using it would need a cruise multiplier that nothing in the listing supports, so it would be a second guess rather than a substitution.
